choices.text: An operation that leaves a molecule indistinguishable from, and superimposable on, its original position
Any motion of a molecule, such as a vibration
choices.why: A symmetry operation must leave the molecule looking exactly as it did before: indistinguishable and superimposable.

choices.text: A chemical reaction that keeps the molecule's shape
choices.why: Symmetry operations are geometric: rotations, reflections, inversions. They don't change the molecule chemically.

choices.text: The point, line, or plane that an operation is performed about
choices.why: That's a symmetry element. The operation is what's done with respect to it.

explanation: A symmetry operation is performed on a molecule and leaves it indistinguishable and superimposable on its original position. Symmetry operations are performed with respect to symmetry elements: points, lines, or planes.

prompt: A water molecule is rotated by 180° and looks exactly the same. In this example, what are the symmetry operation and the symmetry element?

choices.text: The operation is the rotation; the element is the axis of rotation
The operation is the axis; the element is the rotation
choices.why: This is reversed. The element is the geometric object (here an axis), and the operation is what's done about it (the rotation).

choices.text: Both are the water molecule
choices.why: The operation is the 180° rotation, and the element is the C2 axis it's performed about.

choices.text: The operation is a reflection; the element is a mirror plane
choices.why: This example is a rotation, about a C2 axis. (Water does have mirror planes too.)

explanation: In the 180° rotation of water, the symmetry operation is the rotation and the symmetry element is the axis of rotation. A 180° rotation is called a C2 operation.

prompt: Which of these is not one of the five types of symmetry operation?

choices.text: Translation
Inversion
choices.why: Inversion, through a center of symmetry, is one of the five.

choices.text: Improper rotation
choices.why: Improper rotation (S_n), a rotation followed by a reflection, is one of the five.

choices.text: Identity
choices.why: Identity (E), doing nothing, is one of the five, and every molecule has it.

explanation: The five types of symmetry operation are identity (E), reflection (σ), inversion (i), proper rotation (C_n), and improper rotation (S_n). Moving a molecule to a new place isn't one of them.

prompt: A C_n rotation turns a molecule by 360°/n. By how many degrees does a C6 operation rotate a molecule?
explanation: A C_n rotation is by 360°/n, so C6 rotates by 360°/6 = 60°. Likewise C2 is 180° and C3 is 120°.

prompt: A molecule has both C2 and C4 axes. Which is its principal axis?

choices.text: The C4 axis, because it has the highest order
The C2 axis, because 180° is the larger rotation
choices.why: The principal axis is the one of highest order (largest n), not the largest angle. C4 is higher order than C2.

choices.text: Whichever axis passes through the most atoms
choices.why: The principal axis is defined by order: the highest-order proper rotation axis, here C4.

choices.text: Neither: only molecules with a C3 axis have a principal axis
choices.why: Any molecule with proper rotation axes has a principal axis: the one of highest order.

explanation: The principal axis of a molecule is its highest-order proper rotation axis. If a molecule has C2 and C4 axes, the C4 is the principal axis.

prompt: How is a horizontal mirror plane (σh) oriented?

choices.text: Perpendicular to the principal axis
Containing (parallel to) the principal axis
choices.why: Planes containing the principal axis are vertical (σv) or dihedral (σd).

choices.text: Parallel to the principal axis and bisecting two C2' axes
choices.why: That describes a dihedral plane, σd.

choices.text: Parallel to the ground, whatever the molecule's axes
choices.why: "Horizontal" is defined relative to the principal axis: a σh plane is perpendicular to it.

explanation: There are three classes of mirror plane: σh (horizontal), perpendicular to the principal axis; σv (vertical), parallel to the principal axis; and σd (dihedral), parallel to the principal axis and bisecting two C2' axes.

prompt: What distinguishes a dihedral mirror plane (σd) from a vertical one (σv)?

choices.text: A σd plane bisects two C2' axes; both kinds contain the principal axis
A σd plane is perpendicular to the principal axis
choices.why: A plane perpendicular to the principal axis is horizontal (σh). σd and σv both contain the principal axis.

choices.text: A σd plane doesn't contain any atoms
choices.why: The defining feature in the section is that σd planes bisect two C2' axes.

choices.text: There is no difference
choices.why: Both contain the principal axis, but dihedral planes also bisect two C2' axes.

explanation: Vertical (σv) and dihedral (σd) planes are both parallel to the principal axis; dihedral planes also bisect two C2' axes.

prompt: Which shape lacks an inversion center?

choices.text: A tetrahedron
An octahedron
choices.why: An octahedron has an inversion center: each vertex has an identical one directly opposite through the center.

choices.text: A square
choices.why: A square has an inversion center at its middle: every corner has an identical one directly opposite.

choices.text: A linear molecule like CO2
choices.why: CO2 has an inversion center at carbon: each oxygen is opposite the other.

explanation: Inversion takes every point (x, y, z) through the center to (−x, −y, −z). Tetrahedra, triangles, and pentagons lack an inversion center, because a vertex is opposite a face or edge rather than an identical vertex.

prompt: What does an improper rotation, S_n, consist of?

choices.text: A C_n rotation followed by reflection through a plane perpendicular to that axis (σh)
A rotation in the wrong direction (clockwise)
choices.why: "Improper" means the rotation is combined with a reflection, not that it turns the other way.

choices.text: A reflection followed by inversion
choices.why: S_n is a rotation by 360°/n followed by reflection through the plane perpendicular to the rotation axis.

choices.text: Two proper rotations about different axes
choices.why: S_n combines one rotation with a reflection through the plane perpendicular to that axis.

explanation: An improper rotation combines a rotation about an axis (C_n) with a reflection through a plane perpendicular to that axis. In short, S_n is equivalent to C_n followed by σh.

prompt: Which molecules have the identity element, E?

choices.text: All molecules
Only molecules with no other symmetry
choices.why: Every molecule has E, whatever else it has; for molecules with no other symmetry, E is all there is.

choices.text: Only symmetric molecules
choices.why: Even the least symmetric molecule has E: doing nothing always leaves it unchanged.

choices.text: Only linear molecules
choices.why: All molecules have the identity element.

explanation: All molecules have the identity element. The identity operation is doing nothing to the molecule: it doesn't rotate, reflect, or invert.
